alignments.note: Adversative δέ rendered by the verse-opening But.
Inflected verb takes its English subject pronoun as a rule 9 helper; head on the lexical verb exhort.
Anarthrous vocative with no supplied address word, so rule 89 does not arise.

The imperative takes *bear with* whole: no Greek preposition governs the genitive, so *with* is the English phrasal verb's own particle and a rule 7 helper on the verb rather than a rule 36 case preposition. 2CO.11.19 `ἀνέχεσθε` → *ye bear with* is the token-identical frame — same lemma, phrasal verb, articular genitive complement — and is unhedged, saying so in terms; 2CO.11.1 twice and 2CO.11.4 keep the particle on the verb likewise, four units to none once this one is brought into line. Splitting *with* onto the article under rule 21 was the earlier reading here and is rejected: rule 21 allocates a case preposition between an article and its own noun, not between a noun phrase and the verb governing it, and it forbids hanging a bare case preposition on an article that already carries its determiner.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19; the *with* belongs to the phrasal verb at s005 and does not ride here.
Head noun stands bare, its determiner taken by the article.
Rule 23: the ASV gives exhortation no determiner, so this article has no the to anchor and realizes nothing.
Rule 21's determinerless clause: the case preposition of stays with the noun, headed on the noun.
Intensifying καί in καὶ γάρ; the ASV writes no word for it, giving only for. Decided on the English alone as rule 65 requires.
Subject and auxiliary are rule 9 helpers; head on the lexical verb written.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition unto riding along under rule 21.
Rule 36: the preposition governing the phrase is realized by in, not absorbed into the verb.
Substantival adjective expanded with the generic noun words; rule 17's generic-noun clause keeps the head on few.

review_notes: All 15 source and 20 target ids partitioned exactly once.

Two unrepresented units: the second article (s008) under rule 23 and the intensifying καί of καὶ γάρ (s010) under rule 65. A reference comparison may report the καί as a disagreement; the ASV writes no word for it.
The only materially contested unit is bear / with the: rule 36 puts the genitive-licensed with on the article rather than treating bear with as a phrasal verb.
